cells.tense: The whole build is here and you are standing in it, hands on it, pleased and unguarded.
cells.ask: Offer to meet one ordinary moment as if you had never met it before, with no plan for it, and notice what the freshness gives back.
cells.core:
When this part of a life is going well, you build from your own grain instead of someone else's blueprint, and others can feel that it comes from you. You carry what you've made without apologizing for it or holding it over your own head as proof. The thing and the person who made it are the same person — nothing performed, nothing dimmed to fit the room, nothing inflated to fill it either. You can set the finished work down, pick it back up, and it still reads as yours either way.

Meeting an ordinary moment as if for the first time doesn't step away from what you built. It keeps what you built awake and open, so the freshness feeds the thing instead of replacing it.
cells.sheetLine: You built it with your whole self and you are standing in it, unguarded.
cells.verb: carrying what your whole self has become
cells.place: in the part of life where you become what you are

cells.tense: The finish line keeps moving ahead of you and you are sprinting to a version of it that isn't here yet.
cells.ask: Let yourself be seen in one thing you're already good at, without showing anyone you deserve it, and see what comes back.
cells.core:
At its best, this is the part of your life that carries finished work easily and lets the next thing arrive when it arrives. You can hold what you made loosely, set it down, and still know it's yours. That ease is what lets the making keep going without grinding you down, and it's what lets other people stand near your work without feeling managed by it.

What you're doing instead is treating what you made as never finished, so the load just moves forward with you and nothing here ever gets to be real. Being seen in work that's already complete, without building a case for why you merit it, lets it stand where it is instead of where you keep pushing it.
cells.sheetLine: You keep outrunning what you already made.
cells.verb: carrying what your whole self has become
cells.place: in the part of life where you become what you are

cells.tense: You stopped at the edge of becoming what you are, and you are still standing at that edge.
cells.ask: Let one person know you — not your work, not your opinions — and stay for whatever comes back, and notice what opening gives back.
cells.core:
This is the part of a life where your own shape is meant to show in how you live and work — visible without explanation, without strain, without a pitch attached. Others read you clearly because you're not hiding the grain of who you are under the output. It runs steady and quiet, and it's the thing people around you actually trust when they want the real version of you.

What's stopped is the showing. What is real in you is still real; it just isn't reaching the surface where anyone can meet it. Trying harder at becoming doesn't reopen that. Letting one person actually know you, and receiving whatever comes back, is what starts it moving again.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped showing what is real in you and you have not started again.
cells.verb: carrying what your whole self has become
cells.place: in the part of life where you become what you are

cells.tense: You are becoming what you are without saying so, letting it read as something else.
cells.ask: Say out loud, to yourself or someone, the simplest true thing you are becoming, and let the saying be enough.
cells.core:
When this part of a life is working, the shape of who you are is doing the choosing — what you take on, what you turn down, who you spend your days with — and it names itself as it goes. The making is visible as yours. Others can see the person, not just the output, and nothing has to be argued for to be seen.

It is already running. You pick, you refuse, you build the day around some real grain of yourself, and then you file it under luck, or circumstance, or simply how things are. The becoming continues without your claim on it. Naming the simplest true thing you are becoming, once, hands it back to you where you can hold it.
cells.sheetLine: You are becoming something. You have not called it yours.
